extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 named entity data
extraction.description: A dataset for language-independent named entity recognition containing English and German text annotated with four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was sourced from existing text corpora (Reuters Corpus for English and ECI Multilingual Text Corpus for German). It was then preprocessed using tokenizers, part-of-speech taggers, and chunkers, followed by manual named entity tagging at the University of Antwerp.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of English news stories from the Reuters Corpus and German newspaper articles from the Frankfurter Rundshau (part of the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 1996 to August 1997 for the English data, and August 1992 to December 1992 for the German data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging was performed manually at the University of Antwerp, primarily following MUC conventions with the addition of a MISC category for names not fitting other categories.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, tuning parameters (validation/development), and testing learning methods.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Linguistic preprocessing was applied to the raw data, including tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and chunking for all data. The German data was additionally lemmatized.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German1. For each of the languages there is a training file, a development file, a test file and a large file with unannotated data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus... Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: This corpus consists of Reuters news stories... The portion of data that was used for this task, was extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: This corpus consists of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. [...] All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The learning methods were trained with the training data. The development data could be used for tuning the parameters of the learning methods. [...] trained on the training data and tested on the test data.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The participants were given access to the corpus after some linguistic preprocessing had been done: for all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. [...] The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger
